entries.title: Sold-out refusals show a clear message instead of a sticky error toast
entries.summary: When staff apply a credit, record an offline payment, or change a ticket on a registration that is refused because a ticket or pool is sold out, a plain inline message now appears instead of a persistent red **"Request failed"** support toast. When the refusal is caused by an expired hold, the message reads: "Last seat is sold out: this order's hold ran out and the place was sold to someone else. Nothing was charged or recorded; cancel the order or move the registration to another ticket."

where.path: Registration → Orders → [order] → Apply credit / Record a payment; Registration → Registrants → [registrant] → Change ticket

entries.use_case: Staff managing orders at or near capacity no longer see a confusing technical error banner when a seat sells out between steps. The actionable message tells them exactly what happened and what to do next — cancel the order or move the registration to another ticket — without needing to contact support.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports seeing a sticky red 'Request failed' toast on Apply credit or Record a payment, or asks why the error message referenced the wrong action after retrying.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) with paid tickets or shared capacity pools.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Orders → [order] → Apply credit / Record a payment; Registration → Registrants → [registrant] → Change ticket
internal.gotchas: The fix only suppresses the support toast for 409/422 responses that carry a structured error code (e.g. sold_out). 500s, network failures, and uncoded errors still show the support toast as before.
internal.talk_track: If a ticket sells out between when a staff member opens an order and when they try to apply a credit or record a payment, they now see a clear plain message explaining what happened and what to do — no more sticky red banner that blocks subsequent error messages.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that sold-out refusals on Apply credit, Record a payment, and Change ticket surface a plain message (not a support toast), and explain the hold-expired variant of the sold-out message.

entries.title: Contacts' Related Sessions now includes sessions where the contact is the Submitter
entries.summary: In a contacts table, **Related → Sessions** now surfaces sessions where the contact is set as the **Submitter** (`submitted_by_contact_id`), not only sessions where they hold a participant seat. A contact who both submitted and speaks on a session receives a combined **Submitter** badge alongside their participant role (e.g. **Speaker, Submitter**). The chevron count and the related-records export reflect the Submitter role as well. Filtering by participant status (e.g. **Accepted**) correctly excludes submitter-only sessions.

where.path: Contacts → [contact row] → Related → Sessions

entries.use_case: When a contact submitted a session on behalf of a speaker but is not listed as a participant, their Related Sessions panel previously showed nothing — making it look like they had no connection to the session. With this fix, organizers can see every session a contact is tied to, whether as a participant or as the person who submitted it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a contact's Related Sessions panel is missing sessions they know the contact submitted, or when they ask why the submitter shown in the session sidebar does not appear in the contact's related records.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who uses the Submitter field on sessions and relies on the Related Sessions view on contacts to track involvement.
internal.gotchas: A submitter-only row carries no participant status and no role ID, so filtering by participant status (e.g. Accepted) will drop submitter-only sessions from the list — this is intentional and correct behaviour. The 'Submitters' section in the session sidebar lists record owners (Module_Record_Owners / users), which is a separate concept and is not affected by this change.
internal.talk_track: If a contact submitted a session but isn't a speaker or chair on it, their Related Sessions tab now shows that session with a Submitter badge, and the count in the chevron includes it.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the Submitter (submitted_by_contact_id) appears in the contact's Related Sessions view with a Submitter badge, explain that submitter-only rows carry no participant status, and clarify the difference between the session Submitter field and the Submitters section in the session sidebar (which lists record owners).
draft.why_use_it: The session submitter is often a key contact — a department coordinator, a speaker manager, or the speaker themselves — and tracking which sessions they submitted is essential for follow-up and reporting. The Related Sessions view on a contact lets you see all sessions that person is connected to without leaving the contact record, so you can quickly understand their full involvement in the program.

entries.title: Related Sessions table shows Role column and updates immediately after Add to session
entries.summary: In the contacts table with **Related** turned on, the **Sessions (participant or submitter)** relation type now shows a **Role** column (replacing "Relation") that displays each contact's role badge on the session. After using **Add to session**, the related-sessions rows and chevron counts appear instantly — no 30-second wait for the cache to expire.

where.path: Contacts → (contacts table) → Related → Sessions (participant or submitter)

entries.use_case: When an organizer adds one or more contacts to a session, the related-sessions panel now reflects the change right away, so they can confirm the assignment without refreshing or waiting. The Role column also makes it clear at a glance whether each contact is a Speaker, Moderator, Chairperson, or another role on each session.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that sessions don't appear under contacts after using Add to session, or asks why the column says 'Relation' instead of showing the role.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Related Records panel on the contacts table with sessions configured.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → (contacts table) → Related → Sessions (participant or submitter)
internal.gotchas: The Submitter role badge will only appear once the companion API PR (#4916) ships; until then, only seat-based roles (Speaker, Moderator, etc.) show under Role. Other relation types (Submissions, Groups, Sponsors/Exhibitors) still show the Relation column header — that is intentional.
internal.talk_track: After adding contacts to a session, their session rows and counts now appear immediately in the Related panel. The column is also renamed Role so you can see each person's role on the session at a glance.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Related Records panel in the contacts table, including the Sessions (participant or submitter) relation type, the Role column for participation relations, and how the panel refreshes after Add to session.

entries.title: Click anywhere on a toolkit card to open the tool or its setup page
entries.summary: On the event home **Your toolkit** section, the entire card is now clickable — not just the small footer link or button. Clicking an in-use tile opens the tool (same as **Open →**); clicking a ready tile opens its set-up page; clicking a gated (Beta/Preview/not in plan) tile opens the event's **Early Access** page. Footer buttons such as **Open**, set-up CTAs, and **Request beta** still work independently. Cards also gain an accent border and shadow on hover.

where.path: Event home → Today → Your toolkit

entries.use_case: Organizers can now click anywhere on a toolkit card to jump straight to the tool or its setup page, reducing the precision needed to navigate from the event home dashboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions the event home feels hard to navigate or they didn't realise they could open tools from the toolkit section.
internal.who_should_get_it: All organizers — this is on by default for every event.
internal.gotchas: Footer buttons (Open, Request beta, Join preview) still fire their own actions and are not overridden by the card link. Gated tiles navigate to Early Access, not the tool itself — some gated routes (e.g. Clips without Marketing) redirect further to a module overview.
internal.talk_track: You can now click anywhere on a toolkit card — not just the small footer link — to open the tool or start setup. Gated tiles take you straight to Early Access so you can turn on a preview or request a beta.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that the entire toolkit card is clickable and describe where each tile state (in-use, ready, gated) navigates to.
draft.why_use_it: The **Your toolkit** section on the event home gives organizers a single place to see every available tool, its status, and what to do next. Clicking a card takes you directly where you need to go — whether that is a live tool, a setup flow, or the Early Access catalogue — so you spend less time hunting through the sidebar and more time running your event.

entries.title: Ready Room desktop app gets its own page in Apps
entries.summary: A dedicated **Apps → Ready Room** page is now available at both org and event scope. It shows macOS, Windows x64, and Windows ARM download buttons (led by the visitor's OS), a carousel of eleven in-app screens with captions, a **When to use it vs the browser console** comparison, a **Getting a room set up** section with a link to the event's **Live Transcribe → Invites**, and a **Watch the 4-minute walkthrough** button. A **Ready Room** tile also appears in **Your toolkit** on the event home with a "Download the app" prompt.

where.path: Apps → Ready Room; Event home → Your toolkit → Ready Room

entries.use_case: AV and operations teams can find, download, and learn about the Ready Room desktop app without leaving Sessionboard — the page surfaces the right installer for their machine, walks through every screen, and links directly to the event's Live Transcribe invites so they can get a room running in one flow.

cs_action.note: Download buttons only light up once the S3 bucket for releases is provisioned and a release is tagged. Until then the page shows a placeholder note instead of dead buttons — no customer-facing breakage.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is setting up Live Transcribe and asks how their AV crew should run it from the room machine, or when they ask where to download Ready Room.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Live Transcribe with dedicated room machines or AV staff on-site.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Ready Room (org or event sidebar)
internal.gotchas: Download buttons are inactive until the S3_BUCKET_READY_ROOM_RELEASES environment variable is set and a release is published in the lennd/sessionboard-ready-room repo. The toolkit tile is passive — it never counts toward adoption metrics and is never surfaced as the next recommended setup step.
internal.talk_track: Ready Room now has its own page inside Sessionboard. Your AV team can download the right installer for their machine, watch a 4-minute walkthrough, and jump straight to Live Transcribe invites — all from Apps → Ready Room.

draft.docs_gap: The guide exists but should confirm that the in-product page's OS-detection logic matches the install instructions, and add a note that the download buttons require a published release to be active.
draft.why_use_it: The Ready Room desktop app runs on the room machine and gives AV staff a dedicated station view for session files, live transcription, caption overlay, and Focus Mode — all without a browser. Install it on each room machine to keep the crew focused on what is happening in the room rather than managing a full browser console. It works offline when the network drops and syncs automatically when connectivity returns. Use it alongside the browser-based Live Transcribe Console when you need both a room-level station and a multi-room overview.

entries.title: Cancelling a registration from the drawer now promotes the waitlist
entries.summary: When a staff member cancels a registration using the **Cancel** button inside an open registrant record (**Registrants** › open a registration), the freed seat is now offered to the next person — or group — on the waitlist, exactly as the bulk status action already did. A primary registrant and their guests are promoted together or not at all.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → open a registration → Cancel

entries.use_case: When an event is at capacity and staff cancel a registration one at a time from the registrant drawer, waitlisted attendees are now automatically moved up — no need to use the bulk status action to trigger promotion.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that cancelling from the registrant drawer left waitlisted people stuck even though seats were free.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration with ticket capacity limits and a waitlist.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Registrants → open a registration → Cancel
internal.gotchas: No cancellation email is sent to the cancelled registrant — this matches the previous behaviour and is intentional. Promotion emails, if configured, fire as normal. Concurrent cancellations by two staff members at the same time are handled safely.
internal.talk_track: Cancelling a single registration from the drawer now triggers waitlist promotion the same way the bulk action does, so you don't have to remember to run a separate step.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the Cancel button inside an open registrant record triggers waitlist promotion (including promoting a primary and guests together), and that no cancellation email is sent to the cancelled registrant.
draft.why_use_it: Registration lets you cap ticket capacity and hold a waitlist so no seat goes to waste. When a confirmed registrant cancels, the next eligible person — or a primary registrant and their guests as a group — is automatically promoted to confirmed, keeping your event full without manual intervention.

entries.title: Retry payment with a new card after a declined or refused charge
entries.summary: After a declined card or a sold-out refusal, clicking **Pay $…** on the registration checkout now reopens the card entry form so the buyer can enter a different card. Previously, the form silently resubmitted the rejected card token, leaving the buyer stuck with no way to pay without reloading the page and losing their pending order.

where.path: Registration checkout → Pay $… (public registration form and CFP fee payment)

entries.use_case: When a registrant's card is declined or their held seat sells out before payment completes, they can immediately enter a new card without reloading the page and losing their pending order — reducing abandoned checkouts caused by payment failures.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that registrants are stuck after a declined card and have to reload the page to try again.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration with a Spreedly payment gateway (paid tickets or CFP fees).
internal.gotchas: Affects both the public Registration GatewayPayButton and the SitePortal SpreedlyPaymentButton used for CFP submission fees. If a seat sells out between the hold and payment, the buyer sees a sold-out message after entering the new card — this is expected and correct behaviour.
internal.talk_track: If a registrant's card is declined, the card form now reopens automatically so they can try a different card right away — no page reload needed, and their pending order stays intact.

draft.docs_gap: The payments guide should note that after a declined or refused charge the card form reopens automatically so registrants can try a different card without losing their pending order.

entries.title: Publish field events and webinars to Luma and LinkedIn Events
entries.summary: Field events and webinars can now be published to **Luma** and **LinkedIn Events**. Connect either one from the new **Event channels** category in **Apps**, then turn it on under **Publish to** in the event's settings. Registrations from Luma and LinkedIn come back as attendees in the same approval queue, and **People** gets a **Source** column and filter so you can see where each person signed up.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access (our team sets it up with you); then Apps → Event channels → connect Luma (a Luma Plus calendar API key) or LinkedIn Events (sign in, pick your company page, allow posting as the page); then the event's Settings → Publish to

where.path: Apps → Event channels → Luma / LinkedIn Events; field event or webinar form → Publish to; field event Overview → Channels; field event People → Source; field event Settings → Channels

entries.use_case: Teams that also list field events or webinars on Luma or LinkedIn can publish once from Sessionboard, keep the listing in sync as details change, and get every registration back in one attendee list and approval queue, with no manual imports and no double-booked seats.

cs_action.note: Early Access and super-user only for now: the channels UI is visible to Sessionboard staff in orgs with Field Events Early Access. Luma needs the customer's calendar on Luma Plus. LinkedIn ads (Promote) and Matched Audiences are built but wait on LinkedIn approvals (Advertising API Standard, Matched Audiences); until then they show 'Waiting on LinkedIn approval'. The LinkedIn registration form needs staff to switch on 'Registration form' for the connection, then a reconnect.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running field events or webinars asks how to avoid manually importing registrations from Luma or LinkedIn, or when a demand-gen team asks about LinkedIn ad targeting from Sessionboard attendee data.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Field Events (gatherings) or Webinars beta who actively use Luma or LinkedIn Events for promotion and registration.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Event channels → Luma / LinkedIn Events; field event Settings → Channels
internal.gotchas: LinkedIn freezes an event once it starts (later edits stay in Sessionboard), and changing in person ↔ online, the organizer page or the registration choice before the start means deleting and re-creating the LinkedIn event. LinkedIn can't decline an RSVP through the API, so a declined person may still show as attending on LinkedIn. Matched Audiences only add people (no removals yet). Registration-form → Luma question mapping is partial (consent and company). Tested locally and on dev without live Luma/LinkedIn accounts; QA on dev is tracked in SB-10435 / SB-10437 once SB-10701's setup is done.
internal.talk_track: You can publish your field event or webinar to Luma and LinkedIn Events straight from Sessionboard. It stays in sync as you edit, and anyone who registers on Luma or LinkedIn lands in your attendee list and approval queue, with a Source column showing where they came from.

entries.title: Export the Builds list and label builds with custom admin statuses
entries.summary: On a review plan's **Builds** tab you can now export the builds the **Status** filter shows to CSV or XLSX, one row per presenter or alternate, and label builds with your own **build statuses**: admin-only labels under Submitted, Approved or Declined that team leads never see. Manage them under **Program Settings → Build statuses**, also reached from **Manage statuses** on the Builds tab.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → (Review plan) → Builds → Options → Export .CSV / .XLSX; Program → Settings → Build statuses (custom status management)

entries.use_case: Program teams that need to report on build progress can export the full Builds list — with scores, reasons and timing — directly to a spreadsheet. Custom build statuses let admins track internal workflow states (such as "Needs contract" or "Confirmed") on top of the standard lifecycle without exposing those labels to team leads.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: both are there for any review plan round with Enable Reviewer Session Builds on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to report on build progress, share build data with stakeholders, or track internal workflow states on builds without exposing them to team leads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessions 2.0 Review plans with session builds enabled.
internal.staff_path: Program → Evaluation → (Review plan) → Builds → Options → Export .CSV / .XLSX; Program → Settings → Build statuses (custom status management)
internal.gotchas: A label can only be set on a build in its own status (Submitted, Approved or Declined) and comes off when the build is approved, declined, returned or resubmitted; it never changes the build's status. A status's category can't change while builds use it; archiving it removes the label. Build statuses only appears in Program Settings once a review plan in the event has Build turned on. Export needs the review plan export permission, setting a label needs edit, and the Builds tab needs view.
internal.talk_track: You can now export the full Builds list to a spreadsheet — with scores, timing and any custom labels — and use custom build statuses to track internal workflow states on builds without your team leads ever seeing them.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section covering session builds: the Builds tab, the Export action and its column schema, and how to create and apply custom build statuses at the event level.
draft.why_use_it: Session builds let your program team assemble speaker lineups from reviewed abstracts and move them through a structured approval lifecycle. Custom build statuses give admins a private layer of labels — scoped to submitted, approved or declined — so internal workflow states stay visible to the program team without surfacing to team leads or reviewers. The export brings every build, its members, scores, timing and labels into a spreadsheet so you can report on progress, share data with stakeholders or reconcile decisions outside Sessionboard.

entries.title: Registration tickets and workshops can no longer be oversold under concurrent checkouts
entries.summary: Concurrent registrations can no longer exceed ticket, shared-capacity-pool, or free-workshop seat limits. A buyer who returns to pay after their 15-minute hold lapsed and the seat was resold now receives a **Sold out** error before any payment is attempted, rather than being charged into an oversold event. Waitlist auto-promotion also respects capacity under concurrency.

where.path: Registration → Overview; Registration → Tickets & Pricing; public checkout

entries.use_case: Events with high-demand tickets or shared capacity pools (e.g. two fee types drawing from one seat count) can now open registration to large audiences without risking oversold inventory. Buyers who sit on a lapsed hold are turned away cleanly before their card is charged.

cs_action.note: Buyers whose 15-minute hold lapsed and whose seat was resold now get a 409 sold_out before any charge instead of a successful charge. web-ui-v2#1291 (Add a registration sends an Idempotency-Key per attempt) belongs to the same hardening set and is listed in shipped.prs, so the entry goes live only when both are deployed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports oversold tickets after a busy registration open, or asks about shared capacity pool reliability under load.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) with capacity-limited tickets, shared capacity pools, free workshops, or waitlist auto-promotion.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Tickets & Pricing → capacity fields; Registration → Registrants (check confirmed count vs. capacity)
internal.gotchas: Companion PRs #4901 (idempotency) and #4902 (webhooks) plus web-ui-v2#1291 are part of the same hardening set. A charge left pending (ACH, or a card result the gateway has not confirmed) keeps its seats counted while it is in flight; the payment reconciler (web-api #4912) escalates it to Needs review and releases those seats 240 hours (10 days) after the attempt for ACH, 24 hours for cards. Admin 'Offer a place' and bulk status → confirmed remain intentional overrides and are not blocked by this fix.
internal.talk_track: Ticket and workshop capacity is now enforced even when hundreds of buyers check out at the same moment. If someone's hold expires and the seat sells to someone else, they see a sold-out message before their card is charged — no more oversold events.

draft.docs_gap: The shared-capacity section of the Tickets & Pricing guide should document that all fee types sharing a pool are locked together during checkout, and explain the sold-out behaviour when a hold lapses and the seat is resold before payment.
draft.why_use_it: Registration enforces seat limits atomically so that simultaneous checkouts, shared-pool fees, free workshops, and waitlist promotions all respect the capacity you set. When a ticket sells out, buyers receive a clear sold-out response rather than a successful charge into an oversold event.

entries.title: Expo Sales: build the hall faster, keep every booth sale safe, and sell from the map
entries.summary: Floor Maps is now **Expo Sales**. Start a map from a venue starter or import the plan (ExpoFP, Map Your Show or eShow link, DXF with booth detection, SVG, PDF page or image); merge booths into L and T shapes, copy rows, multi-select, bulk edit, renumber by clicking and price by area; draw **walkways** and sponsor images; restore any save from **Version history**; and print or download the hall. Saving the designer never changes a booth's hold, reservation, sale or exhibitor, **Expo → Booth sales** has a new **Map** tab, and **Clone Event** now copies floor maps as drafts with booth sales reset.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Expo Sales → Request access (or Request beta on the Expo Sales tile in Your toolkit)

where.path: Expo → Floor plan (also Publish → Floor Maps); Expo → Booth sales → Map

entries.use_case: Exhibit teams can redraw the hall right up to move-in without losing a single hold or sale, and sales reps can talk a buyer through the floor on the Map tab and hold the booth they point at. Starting from a template or last year's ExpoFP or Map Your Show plan turns days of drawing into minutes.

cs_action.note: Beta, per event. Staff turn on floor_maps (Expo Sales card) and expo for the event after the request; the Early Access card was hidden before and is now listed as Expo Sales.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer with an exhibit hall or poster hall, anyone selling booths on a spreadsheet or an ExpoFP / Map Your Show contract, and every renewal of a show that cloned last year's event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Trade-show and association customers with exhibitors or sponsors, especially those already paying a separate floor-plan vendor.
internal.staff_path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access: Expo Sales (floor_maps) and Expo; then Expo → Floor plan
internal.gotchas: Status and exhibitor edits in the designer Inspector save immediately as booth-sales writes; a hall save or version restore never changes them. Deleting or merging a booth that is held, reserved, sold or on a live application is refused with the booth numbers named; release it in Booth sales first. Version history keeps the newest 200 saves per hall and coalesces a user's saves within 10 minutes. Booth detection is DXF only (closed shapes with a number inside); PDF, SVG and images are backgrounds. Cloned maps come across as drafts, booths all Available, image sponsors and version history not copied.
internal.talk_track: Expo Sales puts the floor plan and booth sales in one place. Start from a template or import last year's plan, reshape it whenever you like, and every hold and sale stays exactly where it is. Your reps sell from the same map exhibitors pick from, and next year's event clones the hall in one step.

entries.title: Attendee floor map on the web, embeddable, with step-free directions; exhibitors pick booths on the real plan
entries.summary: Every published floor map is now an attendee map on the event's Site at **/map/<event ID>** — search, exhibitors by category, saved booths, share links and walking directions along your walkways with an **Accessible route (no stairs)** option. Embed it on any page with one script tag, add `?here=` to QR codes for You-Are-Here signs, and `?kiosk=1` for a touch screen that resets after 90 seconds. Exhibitors pick their booth on the real published plan, with zoom, every hall and the price, and the Attend app's **My route** follows walkways with a **Step-free route** option.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Expo Sales → Request access, then publish a floor map

where.path: Program Site: /s/<slug>/map/<event ID>; embed script floor-map-embed.js; Exhibit & sponsor page booth step; Attend app → My route

entries.use_case: Attendees find the booth they came for from a link, a QR code on a sign or your own website, with no app to install — and get a step-free route if they need one. Exhibitors see exactly where their booth sits before they book, so fewer calls to the exhibit team.

cs_action.note: No admin screen shows the map link or embed code yet: give customers the URL pattern and snippet from the article. The map 404s until a floor map is published.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees navigate the hall, wants a map on their event website, plans wayfinding signage or kiosks, or asks about accessibility on the show floor.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Expo Sales on an in-person event with an exhibit or poster hall.
internal.gotchas: Shows only published maps and the sponsors/exhibitors the Attend app lists; never prices, holds or reserved state (booth is available or shows its exhibitor). Without walkways, directions are a straight line labelled approximate. Kiosk mode resets after 90 s and never stores saves. Map analytics are anonymous Signals (surface web_map). The booth picker falls back to the simple grid when no map is published. The Attend app half (My route along walkways, Step-free route) is lennd/sessionboard-mobile#116, which ships in the next Attend app store build/EAS update; the release job does not track sessionboard-mobile, so confirm the app build before promoting that part.
internal.talk_track: Your floor plan is now your attendee map too: a link, a QR on every sign, an embed on your website, a kiosk in the lobby — all live from the same booths you sell, with step-free directions built in.

entries.title: Interest Form review plans show only the settings that apply
entries.summary: On an Interest Form review plan, the Overview no longer offers messaging or **Include uploaded files**: file questions reach reviewers through **Visible submission fields**. A round's **Privacy & conflict of interest** offers **Keep reviews visible (read-only) after the deadline**, and the Reviewer view pickers split submission questions from contact questions, including a new **Visible participant fields** list.

where.path: CRM → Interest Forms → [form] → Evaluation → Edit plan

entries.use_case: Committees reviewing year-round speaker proposals now see the answers they need, such as a résumé upload, without hunting for a hidden switch, and can look back at their own scores after the deadline.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reviews Interest Form proposals and asks why reviewers can't see uploaded files or contact details.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Speaker CRM Interest Forms and a review plan on them.
internal.gotchas: File questions are now always offered to invited reviewers as ordinary fields; whether they see one depends on Visible submission fields. Messaging with submitters stays event-plan only.
internal.talk_track: Your Interest Form reviewers now see exactly the questions you tick, files included, and can keep read-only access after the deadline.

entries.title: Points-based review plans apply per-question weights
entries.summary: Scorecard questions show a **Weight** in **Points based** plans too: each question's points are multiplied by its weight before they are added up. Weights already saved on points plans are kept when you edit them.

where.path: Review plan → Rounds → scorecard question → Weight

entries.use_case: Committees that score in points can make the questions that matter most count for more, instead of switching the whole plan to percentages.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer on a points plan asks to weight one criterion more heavily.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running points-based review plans.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Review plans → [plan] → Edit → Rounds
internal.gotchas: Scores do not change for existing plans: stored weights were already applied. Before this, editing a points plan reset weights to 1 on save.
internal.talk_track: Points plans now let you weight questions, the same way percentage plans do.

entries.title: Call for Reviewers lists each person's expertise
entries.summary: The **Expertise** column on a Call for Reviewers people table lists the values each person picked, such as tracks, tags or field options, instead of a count.

where.path: Program → Review → Call for Reviewers → [call] → People

entries.use_case: Organizers can see at a glance who knows what before approving applicants or assigning work.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer recruits reviewers with a Call for Reviewers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Call for Reviewers in Sessions or Awards.
internal.gotchas: Shows — when the person picked nothing.
internal.talk_track: The people table now shows what each reviewer said they know.

entries.title: Word, PowerPoint and Excel files preview in the app
entries.summary: Word, PowerPoint and Excel files now open in Microsoft's Office viewer in the approval drawer, the Files sidebar, submission sidebars and the reviewer Site, including files held for approval. Files over the viewer's limit say they are too large to preview and offer **Download**.

where.path: Publish → Approvals; Program → Submissions → Submission files; review portal

entries.use_case: Reviewers and approvers can read a deck or document where they work, instead of downloading every file.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reviews decks or Word documents for approval or committee review.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer collecting Office files.
internal.gotchas: Limits: 10 MB for Word and PowerPoint, 5 MB for Excel. Held files are read through a signed link that expires after a few hours, so Microsoft's viewer receives a time-limited link.
internal.talk_track: Decks and documents now preview right in the review drawer and on the reviewer Site.

entries.title: File approval workflows can filter on any submission field
entries.summary: **Filter by a submission field** adds conditions on any standard or custom submission field to **Applies to**, step conditions and routing rules in file approval workflows. The Approvals page gains a **Session ID** column, and File Settings and the workflow builder now say submission and participant.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Files → Require approval for submission files → Edit approval workflow

where.path: Program → Settings → Files → Edit approval workflow; Publish → Approvals

entries.use_case: Teams can send files to the right approvers by any answer on the submission, such as a custom topic or sponsor flag, and find a file by its Session ID.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants approvals routed by a custom submission field.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Approvals.
internal.gotchas: Field filters are ANDed and count as one condition. A file uploaded before the workflow existed that matches only through a submission field is not held by the release time.
internal.talk_track: Route file approvals by any submission field, not only track or format.

entries.title: Submission PDFs are emailed, not saved on the submission
entries.summary: With **Generate a submission PDF** on, the PDF is attached to the submitter's confirmation email with a download link, and is no longer saved as a file on the submission, so it stays out of the Files library, reviewer views and integrations.

where.path: Program → Forms → [form] → Form Settings → Submission PDF

entries.use_case: Submitters still get a printable copy of their answers, while reviewers and integrations no longer see a generated PDF mixed in with the real files.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a generated Submission PDF shows among submission files or synced content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Submission PDF on.
internal.gotchas: Existing saved PDFs are removed by a one-time cleanup; links already emailed keep working. The setting's own description in the form builder still says the file is stored on the session.
internal.talk_track: The confirmation PDF goes to the submitter and nowhere else.

entries.title: Set your own sign-in heading for portals and submission forms
entries.summary: **Settings → Portals → Portal Login** has a **Sign-in heading** section: a **Heading** and **Sub copy** that replace **Get started** on the submission form's Sign in step and **Welcome to** on the portal login page.

enable.path: Settings → Portals → Portal Login → Sign-in heading

where.path: Submission form Sign in step; portal login page

entries.use_case: Events that sign people in with a member account can tell them so in their own words, for example "Log in or create an account".

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using SSO asks to change the sign-in wording.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with portal customizations, especially SSO-only events.
internal.gotchas: Plain text, not translated per language. Blank keeps the defaults.
internal.talk_track: You can now write the heading people see when they sign in.

entries.title: Payment Settings no longer needs Awards
entries.summary: **Org Settings → Payment Settings** is available to every organization, with or without Awards, so you can connect a gateway for submission form fees. **Manage Payment Settings** on a form's Payments step opens it directly.

where.path: Org Settings → Payment Settings

entries.use_case: Customers who charge submission fees but don't run awards can connect their gateway themselves.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer without Awards wants to charge a submission fee.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations charging submission form fees without Awards.
internal.gotchas: Opening the page needs org settings permission; adding a gateway needs Manage payment gateways. No more enabling Awards just to reach it.
internal.talk_track: Payment Settings is now in every organization's settings.

entries.title: BlueSnap payment gateway
entries.summary: **BlueSnap** is now a featured gateway under **Add Gateway**. Enter your BlueSnap **API Username** and **API Password**; it takes card payments, and **Test Mode** uses your BlueSnap sandbox account.

enable.path: Org Settings → Payment Settings → Add Gateway → BlueSnap

where.path: Org Settings → Payment Settings

entries.use_case: Organizations whose finance team already processes with BlueSnap can take awards, submission and registration fees through it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their processor is BlueSnap.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that bank with BlueSnap.
internal.staff_path: Org → Settings → Payment Settings → Add Gateway
internal.gotchas: Cards only. Sandbox and production are separate BlueSnap accounts. Credentials are only checked by the $1.00 test charge. If BlueSnap restricts API access by IP, Spreedly's IPs must be allowed.
internal.talk_track: BlueSnap is now one click away in Payment Settings.

entries.title: Add LiveBuzz from Apps yourself
entries.summary: LiveBuzz is listed in **Apps** for every organization. Open it to set it up, then connect your LiveBuzz API key and map events; you no longer need to ask Support to add it.

where.path: Apps → LiveBuzz

entries.use_case: Customers on LiveBuzz can connect it the day they decide to, without a support ticket.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a Clarion or LiveBuzz event asks how to push sessions and speakers there.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose events use LiveBuzz.
internal.gotchas: Organizations that already had it installed are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: LiveBuzz is now self-serve in Apps.

entries.title: Coordinator replies can complete manual tasks
entries.summary: With **Let participants reply to complete tasks** on, a reply to a Coordinator email can now complete any task the participant could mark complete in the portal, including manual tasks. In **Inbox**, a reply that saved answers on an unfinished form reads **Saved from this reply (form not finished yet)** instead of **Completed**.

enable.path: CRM → Coordinator → Settings → Let participants reply to complete tasks

where.path: CRM → Coordinator → Inbox

entries.use_case: Speakers who answer "done" by email get the task ticked off for them, so organizers stop chasing tasks that are already finished.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses the Coordinator and speakers reply to its emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Coordinator.
internal.gotchas: A task past its close date is never completed by reply. Duplicate check cards for the same contact field on two forms are merged.
internal.talk_track: A speaker's "I've done it" reply now actually closes the task.

entries.title: Reviewer message emails open the review Site
entries.summary: When someone writes on a submission's reviewer thread, the email's **Open thread** button takes reviewers to the submission on their review Site, at its Messages section, instead of the admin app.

where.path: Reviewer message emails

entries.use_case: Reviewers reach the conversation in one click instead of hitting a permissions error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports reviewers getting a permissions error from a message email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using messaging with submitters on review plans.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Allow messaging with submitters
internal.gotchas: Event admins still go to the admin session's Messages tab.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers now land on their review Site from message emails.

entries.title: Portal users see the original due date, not the extension
entries.summary: Tasks, forms and file requests show portal users only their **Due Date**. An **Extended Due Date** keeps the item open without changing the date they see, on their task cards, the Tasks list, the weekly digest and the closed message.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Assign Items → Extended Due Date

entries.use_case: Organizers can give a quiet grace period without teaching speakers that every deadline will slip.

cs_action.note: A customer who used Extended Due Date to announce a new deadline should move the Due Date instead.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sets extensions on portal tasks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Extended Due Date on portals.
internal.gotchas: The extension is still honoured for completion; an item past its original date but inside the extension is not shown as past due.
internal.talk_track: Extensions are now a silent grace period.

entries.title: Relative due dates for portal forms and file requests
entries.summary: **Due date relative to assignment** now works on portal forms and file requests as well as tasks: each person gets their own due date, N days after they are assigned or after the assignment email is sent.

enable.path: Portals → [portal] → Edit Tasks → [form or file request] → Due date relative to assignment

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Assign Items

entries.use_case: People added late still get a fair window to submit a form or upload a file, without a deadline that has already passed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer adds speakers on a rolling basis.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with rolling portal assignments.
internal.gotchas: The email option stamps on the live assignment email only, not previews or test sends. Existing dates are kept on re-assignment.
internal.talk_track: Forms and file requests can now count down from when each person is assigned.

entries.title: Co-participants can't see each other's tasks
entries.summary: With **Manage Related Submissions and Participants** on, a portal user can open a co-participant's profile but no longer sees their **Tasks** tab; only their own record shows it.

where.path: Portal → session → Participants → [participant]

entries.use_case: Tasks can hold promo codes and private instructions, so they stay with the person they belong to.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer, especially in the EU, asks what co-speakers can see about each other.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Manage Related Submissions on.
internal.gotchas: Profiles, related submissions and participant edits are unchanged. Session submitters and sponsor team members no longer see speakers' tasks either.
internal.talk_track: Speakers' tasks are private to them.

entries.title: Subsessions Only option for portal editing
entries.summary: A new **Subsessions Only** option under **Manage Related Submissions and Participants** lets people who are only on a subsession edit that subsession and see its parent submission read-only.

enable.path: Portals → [portal] → Configuration → Manage Related Submissions and Participants → Subsessions Only

where.path: Speaker portal → parent session

entries.use_case: Symposium chairs keep control of the parent session while each presenter edits their own talk.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs symposia or panels with subsessions and wants presenters kept off the parent.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using subsessions with portal editing.
internal.gotchas: Off by default. Tasks, files, acceptance and messages on the parent are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Subsession presenters can edit their own talk without touching the symposium.

entries.title: Submitters can edit their saved contact details on a form
entries.summary: **Unique Contact Settings → Allow submitters to edit their existing values** fills a signed-in submitter's own participant row with what is saved on their contact, editable. Changes update the contact; blank fields keep their saved value.

enable.path: Program → Forms → [form] → Participant Information → Unique Contact Settings

where.path: Public submission form → participant step

entries.use_case: Returning speakers stop retyping their bio and title on every submission, and their contact record stays current.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with returning speakers asks for prefilled forms.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Unique Contacts.
internal.gotchas: Only the signed-in person's own row is prefilled; other people's rows follow the read-only and lock settings.
internal.talk_track: Returning speakers now see their saved details, ready to edit.

entries.title: Let submitters withdraw their submission
entries.summary: **Form Settings → Withdrawal → Allow submitters to withdraw their submission** shows **Withdraw submission** in the portal at any status. The submitter can give a reason, the submission moves to **Withdrawn**, and event admins are notified.

where.path: Portal → submission

entries.use_case: Speakers who can no longer come pull their own proposal, with a reason, instead of emailing the team.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer handles a lot of withdrawal emails during review.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running calls for papers.
internal.gotchas: Only the submitter can withdraw, not co-participants. Withdrawal from the portal is one-way; admins can undo it from the session. Independent of Participant Acceptance.
internal.talk_track: Submitters can now withdraw themselves, at any status.

entries.title: Show only some dropdown options on a form
entries.summary: **Customize question → Show only some options on this form** lets each submission form offer its own subset of a dropdown's options, including Track, Format, Level, Language and Tags.

enable.path: Program → Forms → [form] → question ⋯ → Customize question → Show only some options on this form

where.path: Public submission form

entries.use_case: One field can serve several calls, such as a poster form and a workshop form, each offering only the formats that fit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs several forms that should offer different formats or tracks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with more than one submission form.
internal.gotchas: Session and sub-session questions only. Values a submission already holds stay valid.
internal.talk_track: Each form can now offer its own slice of a dropdown.

entries.title: View Submissions shows parent-selection submissions
entries.summary: On a form with **Allow submitters to select a parent session**, **View Submissions** lists each submission under the parent it picked, expanded.

where.path: Program → Forms → [form] → ⋯ → View Submissions

entries.use_case: Organizers see every submission the form card counts, even when they were filed under existing sessions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a form's submissions are missing from View Submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using parent session selection.
internal.gotchas: Status tabs still classify by the parent row.
internal.talk_track: A form's View Submissions now shows everything it collected.

entries.title: Unscored optional questions no longer lower a review score
entries.summary: When a reviewer leaves an optional scorecard question unscored, even with a comment, it is left out of that review's total and of averages, and exports show **–** for it. A real 0 still counts.

where.path: Review plan scores, session Reviews tab, exports

entries.use_case: Reviewers can skip a question that doesn't apply, such as "clinical projects only", without dragging the submission's score down.

cs_action.note: Scores rise on percentage plans where reviewers skipped optional questions; let affected customers know before decisions are made.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a submission's percentage looks low.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with optional questions on percentage review plans.
internal.gotchas: Required questions always count. Awards, Surveys and Attend scoring are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Skipped optional questions are now treated as not applicable.

entries.title: Contacts Source field shows how each contact joined
entries.summary: A **Source** reporting field in Contacts names the submission form, the integration, or **Manual** for how each contact joined the event, and you can filter by it.

where.path: Contacts → Columns → Reporting Fields → Session Fields → Source

entries.use_case: Teams can tell speakers who came through the call for papers from those they added by hand.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks where a contact came from.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with Contacts.
internal.gotchas: Derived, not stored. CSV imports and contacts who existed before they submitted show Manual.
internal.talk_track: See how every contact entered the event.

entries.title: Turn the weekly digest off for one contact
entries.summary: In Contacts, **More → Turn off weekly digest emails** keeps the selected people out of the Monday portal digest, and **Turn on weekly digest emails** brings them back. **Weekly Digest Emails Off** shows who is excluded.

where.path: Contacts → select → More

entries.use_case: VIP speakers or staff who don't want weekly reminders can be left out without building a separate portal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a speaker asks to stop getting the weekly digest.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using portal digests.
internal.gotchas: Per event. Send Portal Summary and every other email still reach them. Not offered on sponsor or exhibitor accounts.
internal.talk_track: One click keeps a contact off the weekly digest.

entries.title: Visit: per-contact registration form and type
entries.summary: The Visit app's **Event Settings** now set a **Default registration form** and **Default registration type**, and **Allow per-contact registration form and type** adds **Visit Registration Form** and **Visit Registration Type** contact fields that override them per person.

enable.path: Apps → Visit → [mapping] → Event Settings → Allow per-contact registration form and type

where.path: Contacts → Visit Registration Form / Type

entries.use_case: Expos can register VIP speakers, press or partners on their own Visit form or type in the same sync.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Visit customer needs different registration types for different speakers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers syncing to Visit.
internal.gotchas: Off by default. Values not on the expo fall back to the default, and the sync results say which applied.
internal.talk_track: Each speaker can now go into Visit on the right registration.

entries.title: Restrict custom Site pages to reviewers or submitters
entries.summary: Custom Site pages have **Who can see this page**: **Public**, **Reviewers** or **Submitters**. Restricted pages are hidden from the navigation, and their URL asks visitors to sign in or tells them they have no access.

enable.path: Site builder → [custom page] → Who can see this page

where.path: Program Site and awards Site custom pages

entries.use_case: Teams can publish a reviewer guide or submitter instructions on their Site without making them public.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants a page only reviewers or submitters can read.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a Program or awards Site.
internal.gotchas: Org team members always see restricted pages, so test with a reviewer or submitter account.
internal.talk_track: Site pages can now be just for your reviewers or submitters.

entries.title: Reviewer agent summarizes the previous round's comments
entries.summary: A round setting, **Summarize previous round's reviewer feedback with the Reviewer agent**, lets team leads generate a summary of the comments shared from the previous round, with admin approval, roll back and options for who sees it and whether names are left out.

enable.path: Review plan → Rounds → [round] → Summarize previous round's reviewer feedback with the Reviewer agent

where.path: Review portal → submission → prior-round panel → Agent summary

entries.use_case: Chairs in a second round start from the committee's main points instead of reading every comment one by one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs multi-round review with a chairs' round.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with multi-round review plans and the Reviewer agent on.
internal.gotchas: Off by default. Needs the Reviewer agent on, AI features on, comment sharing on in the previous round, and at least 2 shared comments. Never changes scores or decisions.
internal.talk_track: The Reviewer agent can now brief your round 2 chairs.

entries.title: Session choice: let speakers rank existing sessions
entries.summary: A **Session choice** question on submission forms lets submitters browse the sessions you offer, read their details and rank a 1st, 2nd and 3rd choice. Admins see each applicant on the session's **Potential speakers** card.

enable.path: Program → Forms → [form] → Session Information → Session choice → Add question

where.path: Public submission form; session page → Potential speakers

entries.use_case: Events that build the program first can let speakers apply to the sessions they want, and see who is interested in each one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs a call for speakers for predefined sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who plan sessions before recruiting speakers.
internal.gotchas: Applicants are not participants: no acceptance emails, tasks or integration pushes. Newer-builder forms only.
internal.talk_track: Speakers can now apply for your sessions and rank them.

entries.title: Advocacy: share to WeChat
entries.summary: Turn on **WeChat** under a campaign's **Share channels**. **Share to WeChat** gives advocates a QR code of their tracked link to scan in WeChat, the card to download and the caption with the link to copy. The channel mix now shows **Clicks opened in the app** for WeChat, LINE, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Edit campaign (or Quick Launch) → Share console → Share channels → WeChat

where.path: Advocacy campaign Share channels; the advocate's Creator console (card, text and video shares); Analytics → Channel mix → Clicks opened in the app

entries.use_case: Events with speakers or attendees in Greater China can let advocates share where their network actually is, on WeChat, with every click still traced back to the person who shared.

cs_action.note: Off by default: WeChat is opt-in per campaign and is never added to the default channels. Existing campaigns keep their saved channels.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers with Chinese-speaking speakers or audiences, or anyone asking whether Advocacy works for WeChat.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Advocacy campaigns for events with Greater China audiences.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Edit campaign → Share console → Share channels
internal.gotchas: WeChat has no web share link, so there is no one-tap post: the advocate scans the QR code in WeChat, or downloads the card and pastes the caption. Opening the dialog counts as one share. A WeChat link share shows WeChat's generic preview, not our card. Access from mainland China has not been tested; do not promise it works there. In-app clicks are only counted when the link opens inside the app's own browser.
internal.talk_track: Your advocates can now share to WeChat: a QR code, the card and the caption, all tracked back to them.
